name: process-exec-scrub-cloexec
title: tests(process): pin exec_scrub cloexec-only teardown and pipe release
body:
### What
Pins `exec_scrub`: only cloexec ends are closed, their pipes released, surviving fds stay usable, and the call is idempotent.

### Why it matters
exec must drop cloexec descriptors without touching kept ones. No existing test exercises exec_scrub, so inverting the cloexec predicate or miscounting survives.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `entry.cloexec` -> `!entry.cloexec` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| return `0` instead of `count` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-process --lib exec_scrub_drops`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

name: vfs-overlay-scrub-reuse
title: tests(vfs): scrub unlinked overlay slot before reuse
body:
### What
Pins that an unlinked overlay slot is scrubbed (data zeroed, len reset) before reuse so a fresh overlay never leaks prior bytes.

### Why it matters
Overlay reuse must not expose stale content. Existing tests cover whiteouts but not scrub-on-reuse, so dropping the scrub survives.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| drop `data.fill(0)` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| drop `len = 0` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-vfs --lib unlinked_overlay_slot`.

name: instance-override-resources
title: tests(instance): pin resource overrides and unknown-key rejection
body:
### What
Pins `apply_override` for resources.vcpus/memory_mib and rejection of unknown keys.

### Why it matters
Override arms map keys to fields; a deleted arm silently ignores the override. Existing tests don't pin these arms.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)

name: instance-validate-bounds
title: tests(instance): pin validate vcpu and memory bounds
body:
### What
Pins `validate` resource bounds: vcpus 1..=64, memory 16..=1048576; out-of-range rejected, boundary accepted.

### Why it matters
Bounds are fail-closed config gates; widening them admits invalid configs. Existing tests don't pin the exact edges.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `1..=64` -> `1..=65` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `16..=` -> `15..=` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-instance --lib validate_enforces_vcpu`.

name: core-open-readonly
title: tests(core): pin open/openat read-only admission
body:
### What
Pins open(2)/openat(257) admission to read-only: any write access mode or mutating flag is denied.

### Why it matters
The balanced surface is read-only for opens; widening it would admit writes. Existing tests pin writev/wait4 but not open flags.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| drop O_ACCMODE from open mask | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| openat mask -> 0 | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-core --lib open_admission_is_readonly`.

name: instance-derive-grants
title: tests(instance): derive contract write grant from create-only lists
body:
### What
Pins that a create-only filesystem list still derives the filesystem.** write grant.

### Why it matters
Write authority must follow create capability; dropping the create clause under-grants. Existing tests don't pin this derivation.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
